anchors.name: the fuse going in the building

traces.description: a crack in the cellar and every light on the riser out at once
it was the second floor that went dark and not the whole house
candle smoke on the ceilings of everyone who sat it out

anchors.sceneFact: The fuse went at {T} and the lights on that riser were dead from then until the morning.

anchors.name: the bells at St. Malachy’s

traces.description: the half hours are rung and the whole hours are rung twice

anchors.sceneFact: The bells rang the half hour at {T}. The sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time.

Corrigan was found at Pier 46. The lamp came down with him and the bulb is still warm in its socket, unbroken. The bells rang the half hour at 8:00 PM. The sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time.
The coroner puts death between 7:00 PM and 8:30 PM — two hours of nothing useful. One depressed fracture at the back of the skull. Death was not instant.
A bronze bookend is gone from the walk-up. There is a clean square in the dust where it stood.
Dettweiler puts Corrigan at the Hallam when the lights went, which was 7:30 PM, and alive enough to argue about the weather.
Tramonti was at the Bijou at 8:00 PM and heard a heavy fall and a cry cut short from the direction of Pier 46, while the bells were going.
Dettweiler was at the Bijou at 8:00 PM and heard a heavy fall and a cry cut short from the direction of Pier 46, while the bells were going.
Found at the walk-up: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Ainsworth, endorsed to Corrigan, three months past due.
Brauer says Corrigan told Ainsworth that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at the walk-up: A subpoena naming Corrigan before the grand jury, with Prentiss’s name written in the margin.
Ainsworth says Corrigan said to Prentiss that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Prentiss hired us, and wants it known that Ainsworth owed the victim money, and would rather we started there.
Mosley on Sirkin: Sirkin was asking around for a hundred dollars in a hurry earlier in the week.
Ainsworth on Sirkin: A man nobody knew was waiting for Sirkin at Dolan’s and would not give a name.
Tramonti on Sirkin: Sirkin goes very quiet when the racing wire is mentioned.
Betting slips at Dolan’s in Sirkin’s pocketbook, all of them losers, all of them this month.
A book of markers at Dolan’s with Sirkin’s initials against four of them.
The bookmaker’s runner is found and will say it: Sirkin was at Dolan’s from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM paying off eleven hundred dollars, a dollar at a time, and went nowhere near the killing.
The book at Dolan’s has the payment entered against Sirkin’s name and the time beside it, from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM, in the clerk’s own hand.
Reinhardt on Abramowitz: Abramowitz had taken a drink and had gone to some trouble about the smell of it.
Brauer on Abramowitz: Abramowitz is on a temperance pledge that Abramowitz mentions before anybody asks.
Dettweiler on Abramowitz: Somebody at the Bijou says Abramowitz is in more often than Abramowitz lets on.
A bottle at the Bijou pushed behind the pipes, the seal broken and the level down.
A tab at the Bijou in a name that is not Abramowitz’s, in Abramowitz’s handwriting.
The man behind the counter at the Bijou knows exactly: Abramowitz was on the same stool from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM and was in no condition to walk anywhere, let alone do this.
The tab at the Bijou is dated and timed, from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM, and Abramowitz was there to run it up.
Sirkin on Reinhardt: Reinhardt’s sleeves are buttoned at the wrist in a warm room.
Ainsworth on Reinhardt: Somebody at the Bijou sells what a druggist will not, and Reinhardt knows which door.
Tramonti on Reinhardt: Reinhardt was steady at nine and shaking at seven, and it was not nerves about the police.
A paper of powder at the Bijou, folded the way one particular hand folds them.
A prescription blank at the Bijou signed by a doctor who has been dead since the spring.
The man who sells it at the Bijou gives it up rather than be held: Reinhardt was there from 6:30 PM, and stayed until it took hold.
The doctor Reinhardt used to see confirms the habit and the hour: Reinhardt was at the Bijou from 6:30 PM, and could not have crossed the street unhelped.
Brauer on Ainsworth: Ainsworth’s sleeves are buttoned at the wrist in a warm room.
Dettweiler on Ainsworth: Somebody at the Bijou sells what a druggist will not, and Ainsworth knows which door.
Sirkin on Ainsworth: Ainsworth was steady at nine and shaking at seven, and it was not nerves about the police.
A paper of powder at the Bijou, folded the way one particular hand folds them.
A prescription blank at the Bijou signed by a doctor who has been dead since the spring.
The man who sells it at the Bijou gives it up rather than be held: Ainsworth was there from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM, and stayed until it took hold.
The doctor Ainsworth used to see confirms the habit and the hour: Ainsworth was at the Bijou from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM, and could not have crossed the street unhelped.
Ainsworth on Brauer: Brauer and the victim were heard at the Hallam, and one of them was doing all the talking.
Tramonti on Brauer: Brauer has come into money lately and has no visible way of having come into money.
Mosley on Brauer: The victim had been drawing cash in amounts that did not match anything in the accounts.
An envelope at the Hallam with nothing in it, addressed in the victim’s hand to no one.
A photograph at the Hallam, folded small, of something the victim would have paid to keep folded.
The victim’s bank book settles it: four payments, and Brauer at the Hallam from 6:00 PM collecting the fifth. It is extortion, and an extortionist wants the man alive.
The thing Brauer was holding over the victim turns up, and it was worth more to Brauer every month than once.
